title: Pig Neural Recording and Analysis Workflow
author: Jeffrey Ardell
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2i4gcgw

steps.title: Setup Neural Recording Hardware
steps.instruction: Configure the linear microelectrode array (LMA) and amplification system for neural data acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Record 16 neural channels from 16 electrodes on the LMA (Electrode 1 at the tip, distributed linearly to Electrode 16).
Attach connecting wires of the multichannel electrode, earth, and reference wires to a 16-channel microelectrode amplifier with headstage preamplifier (A-M systems, Inc., model 3600).
Set filters for each channel to 300 Hz to 3 kHz and gain to 5K.
Amplify and convert signals from analog to digital using the CED system.
Assign channels (ICN1, ICN2, ..., ICN16) in the Spike2 acquisition software, where recording from electrode i is assigned to ICNi.

steps.title: Setup Hemodynamic and Reference Monitoring
steps.instruction: Establish reference and pressure monitoring for cardiac activity.

substeps.instruction: Sew a hook electrode to the atrial myocardium to provide a reference right atrial electrogram (RAE) for determining atrial rate and duration.
Record a standard lead II electrocardiogram (EGG).
Insert a 5-Fr Mikro-Tip pressure transducer catheter (Millar Instruments) into the left ventricular chamber via the left femoral artery to measure left ventricular chamber pressure (LVP).

steps.title: Perform Artifact Removal
steps.instruction: Identify and remove simultaneous waves appearing across all 16 channels.

substeps.instruction: Identify electrical stimulation artifacts using the grass channel to determine exact time and shape.
Identify heart electrical-related artifacts using onset detections of atrial and ventricular activities.
Identify unknown source artifacts by selecting a channel with no neural activity and identifying waveforms present on all channels with similar morphology.
Create an event channel based on these identifications and remove artifacts by blanking the signal.

steps.title: Calculate Signal to Noise Ratio
steps.instruction: Determine the SNR for each extracellular action potential.

substeps.instruction: Divide the amplitude of the extracellular action potential by the maximum amplitude of the noise.
Retain only signals with a minimum acceptable SNR of 3 for further analysis.

steps.title: Process Hemodynamic Data
steps.instruction: Derive cardiac metrics from ECG and LVP signals.

substeps.instruction: Derive Heart Rate (HR) in beats per minute from the ECG signal using thresholding to detect each beat and illustrating the HR curve as instant frequency.
Create a dp/dt signal by taking the first derivative of the LVP signal.
Determine dp/dt min/max using the maximum and minimum values of the dp/dt channel.
Create an end systolic LVP curve by detecting the maximum value of LVP at the end of the systolic phase.

steps.title: Perform Spike Sorting
steps.instruction: Classify detected neural spikes into individual neurons.

substeps.instruction: Identify spikes that meet the acceptable SNR criteria.
Classify identified spikes using principal component analysis (PCA) and cluster on measurement analysis to assign a label to each individual neuron.

steps.title: Conduct High-Level Analysis in Matlab
steps.instruction: Transfer sorted spikes and hemodynamic channels to Matlab for advanced processing.

substeps.instruction: Perform Event Triggered Averaging to assess phase-locked neural activity and correlation between firing activity and the cardiac cycle or electrical stimulation.

Analyze significant changes in firing rate by calculating average firing rate over time windows, using a statistical test based on Poisson and Skellam distributions (implemented via R package 'skellam') with significance levels of 1% and 5%.

Assess functional responses to stressors, including: touching RV/LV ventricular surfaces, transient great vessel occlusion (IVC, aorta, or bilateral carotid arteries), or electrical stimulation of cervical vagi (RCV, LCV) or stellate ganglia (RSG, LSG).

Perform Network Analysis using conditional probability to quantify if neurons responding to one stressor (X) also respond to another (Y), calculated as: (number of neurons responding to both X and Y) / (number of neurons responding to X), where a response is defined as P < 0.05.
